payload.claim: `_find_spec_version` picks the committed `.saffron/specs/` blob whose sha256 equals the task's `spec_sha`, which is the whole point of searching git history rather than trusting the worktree — the spec's own notes call this out explicitly ("a spec re-runs only once its `spec_sha` changes", implying multiple distinct committed versions coexist under one spec_id). No test ever commits two different spec texts under the same spec_id: `spec_text()`'s `marker` parameter, which the docstring says exists to vary content, is never passed a non-empty value anywhere in `tests/test_projection.py`, so every spec_id in the suite has exactly one committed version. Deleting the hash check (lines 148-149) so the function returns the first path-matching blob regardless of its content would leave every existing test green, because with only one candidate per id the first match and the hash-correct match are always the same blob.
